# OpenAPI Modifier

> Supports OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1. OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) support has not been tested.

## Usage

### CLI via NPX

```shell
npx openapi-modifier --input=input/openapi.yml --output=output/openapi.yml --config=openapi-modifier.config.js
```

CLI parameters:

| Option   | Description                                                                                              | Example                      | Default                                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |----------------------------------------------|
| `input`  | [**required**] input file, openapi specification/documentation                                          | `input/openapi.yml`          |                                              |
| `output` | [**required**] output file, openapi specification/documentation                                         | `output/openapi.yml`         |                                              |
| `config` | path to the configuration file. For detailed configuration description [see below](#configuration) | `openapi-modifier.config.js` | `openapi-modifier.config.(js\ts\json\yaml\yml)` |
| `verbose` | Show each rule execution and its diff in the console, and save a complete log to a temporary file. | `--verbose` | `false` |
| `minLevel` | Minimum console log level: `0` trace, `1` info, `2` not-important-warning, `3` warning, `4` error, `5` success. | `--minLevel 0` | `2` (unless configured) |

For more details about the configuration file, [see below](#configuration)

If the configuration path is not specified, the default configuration is taken from the `openapi-modifier.config.js` file relative to the launch directory.

You can use configs with the following extensions: `.ts`, `.js`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`.

### CLI

```shell
npm i --save-dev openapi-modifier

openapi-modifier --input=input/openapi.yml --output=output/openapi.yml --config=openapi-modifier.config.js
```

CLI parameters:

| Option   | Description                                                                                              | Example                      | Default                                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |----------------------------------------------|
| `input`  | [**required**] input file, openapi specification/documentation                                          | `input/openapi.yml`          |                                              |
| `output` | [**required**] output file, openapi specification/documentation                                         | `output/openapi.yml`         |                                              |
| `config` | path to the configuration file. For detailed configuration description [see below](#configuration) | `openapi-modifier.config.js` | `openapi-modifier.config.(js\ts\json\yaml\yml)` |
| `verbose` | Show each rule execution and its diff in the console, and save a complete log to a temporary file. | `--verbose` | `false` |
| `minLevel` | Minimum console log level: `0` trace, `1` info, `2` not-important-warning, `3` warning, `4` error, `5` success. | `--minLevel 0` | `2` (unless configured) |

For more details about the configuration file, [see below](#configuration)

If the configuration path is not specified, the default configuration is taken from the `openapi-modifier.config.js` file relative to the launch directory.

You can use configs with the following extensions: `.ts`, `.js`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`.

To investigate unexpected changes, run the CLI with `--verbose`. It prints a diff after each rule, comparing the OpenAPI document before and after that rule, so you can identify which pipeline step caused a change.

### Programmatic Usage

```typescript
import { openapiModifier } from 'openapi-modifier';

(async () => {
    try {
        await openapiModifier({
            input: 'input/openapi.yml',
            output: 'output/openapi.yml',
            pipeline: [
                {
                    rule: 'remove-operation-id',
                    config: {
                        ignore: [],
                    },
                },
            ],
        });

        process.exit(0);
    } catch (error) {
        console.error(error);
        process.exit(1);
    }
})();
```

## Configuration

Create a configuration file (e.g., `openapi-modifier.config.js` or `openapi-modifier.config.ts`) with the following structure:

```javascript
module.exports = {
    // (optional) Logger settings
    logger: {
        verbose: true, // Show each rule and its diff; write a complete log to a temporary file
        minLevel: 0    // Minimum console log level: 0 - trace, 1 - info, 2 - not-important-warning, 3 - warning, 4 - error, 5 - success
    },
    // Path to input OpenAPI specification file
    input: './openapi.yaml',
    // Path to output file
    output: './modified-openapi.yaml',
    // Pipeline of rules to apply (see below for all available rules with configuration examples)
    pipeline: [
        {
            rule: "change-content-type",
            disabled: false, // (optional) Disable rule
            config: {
                map: {
                    "*/*": "application/json"
                }
            }
        }
        // Other rules...
    ]
}
```

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Thanks to the pipeline structure of rules, you can:
> - edit the result of the previous stage with the next stage, thus building a sequence of necessary changes;
> - use rules as many times as needed and in the required sequence;

## Choose a rule

Run `openapi-modifier skill` to read these instructions from the installed CLI.
The following commands return the instructions for each available rule:

- `openapi-modifier skill change-content-type`
- `openapi-modifier skill change-endpoints-basepath`
- `openapi-modifier skill filter-by-content-type`
- `openapi-modifier skill filter-endpoints`
- `openapi-modifier skill merge-openapi-spec`
- `openapi-modifier skill patch-component-schema`
- `openapi-modifier skill patch-endpoint-parameter-schema`
- `openapi-modifier skill patch-endpoint-request-body-schema`
- `openapi-modifier skill patch-endpoint-response-schema`
- `openapi-modifier skill patch-endpoint-schema`
- `openapi-modifier skill remove-deprecated`
- `openapi-modifier skill remove-max-items`
- `openapi-modifier skill remove-min-items`
- `openapi-modifier skill remove-operation-id`
- `openapi-modifier skill remove-parameter`
- `openapi-modifier skill remove-unused-components`

## Available Rules

The relative links below point to files inside the installed `openapi-modifier`
package, for example `node_modules/openapi-modifier/dist-docs/skills/`.
When reading this documentation from CLI stdout, run
`openapi-modifier skill <rule-name>` to view a rule's documentation directly.

| Rule | Short Description |
|------------------------------------------------------------------| ---- |
| [change-content-type](dist-docs/skills/change-content-type.md) | Changes content types in the OpenAPI specification according to the replacement dictionary |
| [change-endpoints-basepath](dist-docs/skills/change-endpoints-basepath.md) | Changes basepaths of endpoints according to the replacement dictionary |
| [filter-by-content-type](dist-docs/skills/filter-by-content-type.md) | The rule allows filtering content types in the OpenAPI specification. It enables explicit specification of which content types should be kept or removed from the specification. The rule applies to all API components, including requests, responses, and common components. |
| [filter-endpoints](dist-docs/skills/filter-endpoints.md) | The rule allows filtering endpoints in the OpenAPI specification based on their paths and methods. It enables explicit specification of which endpoints should be kept or removed from the specification. The rule supports both exact matching and regular expression-based filtering. |
| [merge-openapi-spec](dist-docs/skills/merge-openapi-spec.md) | Merges two OpenAPI specifications into one. Allows merging the current specification with an additional specification from a specified file. Supports working with files in JSON and YAML formats. |
| [patch-component-schema](dist-docs/skills/patch-component-schema.md) | This rule allows modifying the component schema in the OpenAPI specification. |
| [patch-endpoint-parameter-schema](dist-docs/skills/patch-endpoint-parameter-schema.md) | The rule allows modifying the schema of endpoint parameters in the OpenAPI specification. |
| [patch-endpoint-request-body-schema](dist-docs/skills/patch-endpoint-request-body-schema.md) | Rule for modifying the request body schema in OpenAPI specification. Allows to modify the request schema for a specified endpoint. |
| [patch-endpoint-response-schema](dist-docs/skills/patch-endpoint-response-schema.md) | The rule allows modifying the response schema for endpoints in the OpenAPI specification. |
| [patch-endpoint-schema](dist-docs/skills/patch-endpoint-schema.md) | The rule allows modifying the entire endpoint schema in the OpenAPI specification. Unlike other patching rules that work with individual parts of the endpoint (parameters, request body, responses), this rule can modify the entire endpoint structure, including all its components. |
| [remove-deprecated](dist-docs/skills/remove-deprecated.md) | The rule allows removing deprecated elements from the OpenAPI specification. It can remove deprecated components, endpoints, parameters, and properties, while providing the ability to ignore specific elements and display descriptions of removed elements. |
| [remove-max-items](dist-docs/skills/remove-max-items.md) | Removes the `maxItems` property from all schemas in the OpenAPI specification. |
| [remove-min-items](dist-docs/skills/remove-min-items.md) | Removes the `minItems` property from all schemas in the OpenAPI specification. |
| [remove-operation-id](dist-docs/skills/remove-operation-id.md) | Removes operationId from all operations in the OpenAPI specification, except those specified in the ignore list |
| [remove-parameter](dist-docs/skills/remove-parameter.md) | Removes a parameter from an endpoint in the OpenAPI specification |
| [remove-unused-components](dist-docs/skills/remove-unused-components.md) | Removes unused components from the OpenAPI specification. The rule analyzes all component references in the document and removes those that are not used anywhere. |

## Get more information

Run `openapi-modifier skill` to get general configuration instructions and the
list of available rules.

Run `openapi-modifier skill <rule-name>` to get configuration options, examples,
and documentation for a specific rule.

- [Source repository](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier)
- [Target descriptors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/refs/heads/main/docs/descriptor.md)
- [Differences between merge and deepmerge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/refs/heads/main/docs/merge-vs-deepmerge.md)
- [simple-text-file-modifier](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/refs/heads/main/docs/simple-text-file-modifier.md): CLI for modifying text files.

## Usage examples

Browse the [examples directory](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples)
and open the relevant example to inspect its configuration, scripts, input, and output.

- [CLI via NPX](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-cli-simple-npx): run the CLI without installing the package locally.
- [CLI with YAML](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-cli-openapi-yaml): modify a YAML specification from the command line.
- [CLI with JSON](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-cli-openapi-json): modify a JSON specification from the command line.
- [YAML to JSON](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-cli-openapi-yaml-to-json): read YAML and write JSON.
- [JSON configuration](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-cli-simple-json-config): configure the pipeline using a JSON file.
- [API type generation](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-cli-generate-api-types): modify a specification before generating API types.
- [Programmatic usage](https://github.com/itwillwork/openapi-modifier/tree/main/examples/example-package-openapi-yaml): call the package from application code.

## FAQ

- **Why are $ref modifications dangerous?** Because it means that $ref refers to a common part of the schema, and its modification may lead to implicit changes in another part of the specification where $ref is reused, and such a bug will be extremely difficult to catch.
